- requirement: "keep the existing fail-closed path checks"
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py count_identical_failures, the fallback block (lines 2918-2921) and the gate workflow's `FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED` propagation

  EVIDENCE: The cap_applied propagation from the unfiltered older result is not preserved in the fallback block. Existing tests pass because no assertion checks `outputs["fingerprint_cap_already_applied"]` for the bound scenario (test_workflow_failure_heal.py:3903-3908). The cap-block job's `if` predicate (review_autofix.yml:2633) and the comment jq filter (review_autofix.yml:2768-2770) both gate on a current-support match, so older cap markers do not stop the cap-block job from re-running on every new support SHA after the bound. The existing fail-closed "don't re-post cap when one already exists" check is bypassed in this scenario, breaking the contract the issue required to preserve.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2857-2861 and 2912-2921 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The `cap_applied` check filters cap markers by the evaluating run's `support=` value. The new fallback copies only `count`, `fp`, `reason`, `support` and `non_retryable` from the unfiltered result. It does not copy `cap_applied`.
  WHY: A head has used up its re-arm bound (3 recorded support SHAs) and carries a cap comment `support=S3`. A later main commit gives the gate a new verified support SHA S4. The filtered pass counts 0 markers and `cap_applied=false`. The fallback finds the older non-retryable stop, so `rearm=false` and the gate trips the cap. `FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED` stays `false`, so the `fingerprint-cap-block` job runs again. It re-labels, posts another `review-autofix-failure-cap:v1` comment, sends another `identical_failure_cap` heal report and sends another Telegram notice. This repeats once per new support SHA on main, indefinitely, for a head that is already capped. This is the duplicate-noise outcome the bound was meant to prevent. Fix: in the fallback, set `result["cap_applied"] = result["cap_applied"] or older["cap_applied"]`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml; scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Every production caller of `autofix-failure-fingerprint` already passes `--support-sha` explicitly. These are the calls in `review_autofix.yml` (lines 5107, 6512, 6603) and in `scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh` (line 59). An explicit `--support-sha ""` overrides the default. The new env var and default therefore never change production behavior. The only reader is a test, `test_render_failure_marker_records_a_valid_support_sha`.
  WHY: Nothing fails. It adds a second, unused input path for the same value, which could mislead a later maintainer.

=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2920-2921 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: During the recursive call to count_identical_failures to re-arm a capped head, the cap_applied field is not carried over from the older results to the final result dictionary.
  WHY: If the original non-retryable stop had already applied the cap (posted the warning block comment and fired an alert), losing this information may result in redundant cap comments, alerts, or heal-report runs for the same PR head because the system no longer knows the cap was previously applied and fulfilled.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2994 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The AUTOFIX_FAILURE_SUPPORT_SHA environment variable added in this PR is passed to the codex-agent job but is not actually read or used by the production code, which relies on REVIEW_SUPPORT_SHA instead.
  WHY: This adds clutter to the environment without purpose and introduces a confusing inconsistency in interface.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2912-2921; lines 2857-2861 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: After the re-arm bound is reached (`len(recorded_supports) >= DEFAULT_FAILURE_CAP_MAX_REARMS` with no rearm eligible), every new support SHA on `main` causes the cap-block job to run again and post a duplicate cap comment, heal report, and Telegram alert. The fallback block at lines 2912-2921 reads `count`, `fp`, `reason`, `support`, and `non_retryable` from the unfiltered older result, but does NOT propagate `cap_applied`. Combined with the cap_applied loop at lines 2857-2861 which only sets `cap_applied=True` for cap markers matching the support filter, the gate's `FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED` stays `false` for every newer support SHA after the bound.
  WHY: Scenario: head H is capped at support S1 with reason `conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only`. Re-arms at S2 and S3 each fail and add a failure marker, so `recorded_supports={S1,S2,S3}` (3 distinct SHAs). Main advances to S4. The gate calls the helper with `support_sha=S4, current_support_sha=S4`. The support filter excludes every failure and cap marker (none carry `support=S4`), so `result["count"]=0`. The fallback fires (`support` is truthy, `is_valid_sha(current_support)` is true, `count==0`); the recursive `older` call returns `non_retryable=True` plus `cap_applied=True` (because the unfiltered call sees the cap marker under S1), but only the first five keys are copied. `cap_applied` remains False on the outer result. The gate then sets `FINGERPRINT_CAP=true, FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED=false`. The cap-block job's `if` (review_autofix.yml line 2633: `needs.gate.outputs.fingerprint_cap == 'true' && needs.gate.outputs.fingerprint_cap_already_applied != 'true'`) passes. The job's internal jq check at lines 2768-2770 looks for a cap marker matching the current support SHA only, so the older S1/S2/S3 cap markers do not match S4. The job posts another cap comment (line 2852), logs another `AUTOFIX_FINGERPRINT cap=applied` (line 2855), sends another Telegram alert (line 2857+), and dispatches another heal report (line 2880+). Every subsequent main commit while the head stays at this state repeats the noise. Test `test_gate_rearms_a_non_retryable_cap_for_a_new_support_sha` only asserts `outputs["should_run"] == "false"` and `skip_reason == "fingerprint_cap"` for the bound case (test_workflow_failure_heal.py:3903-3908); it does not assert `outputs["fingerprint_cap_already_applied"] == "true"`, so the regression is uncovered.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:4562-4567; review_autofix.yml line 2994 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The argparse default `os.environ.get("AUTOFIX_FAILURE_SUPPORT_SHA", "")` is redundant. Every production caller of `autofix-failure-fingerprint` explicitly passes `--support-sha "${REVIEW_SUPPORT_SHA:-}"` (review_autofix.yml lines 5116, 6520, 6611; scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh line 69), which always overrides the argparse default. The env var is set in the codex-agent env at line 2994 but only matters for the implicit call inside scripts/workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh line 301 (which doesn't pass `--support-sha`); that script could pass it explicitly instead. The dual-channel design (explicit `--support-sha` plus env-var-backed default) makes the contract ambiguous and the env var a dead interface that future readers must trace.
  WHY: No functional failure today, but the env var adds an undocumented second channel for `--support-sha`. Future maintainers who remove `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_SUPPORT_SHA` from the codex-agent env (assuming it is dead, as three production callers already pass the value explicitly) would silently break the call at workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh line 301, where the support filter would default to empty and the report would scan markers from every support version.

  Evidence of absence: The cap_applied propagation from the unfiltered older result is not preserved in the fallback block. Existing tests pass because no assertion checks `outputs["fingerprint_cap_already_applied"]` for the bound scenario (test_workflow_failure_heal.py:3903-3908). The cap-block job's `if` predicate (review_autofix.yml:2633) and the comment jq filter (review_autofix.yml:2768-2770) both gate on a current-support match, so older cap markers do not stop the cap-block job from re-running on every new support SHA after the bound. The existing fail-closed "don't re-post cap when one already exists" check is bypassed in this scenario, breaking the contract the issue required to preserve.
